stops.note: the month of Janus, two-faced god of doorways and beginnings; from 153 BC Roman consuls took office on 1 January, making it the start of the civil year
the Norman French form replaced Old English Æfterra Geola, 'after Yule'
respelled after Latin; England's legal year began on 25 March until the Calendar Act of 1750 moved New Year's Day to 1 January from 1752

current_meaning: the first month of the year
